Make Robot stay the assistant after a restart

After a restart: Android 17 keeps a non-system assistant across a restart only when a default speech recognizer is set, and it never picks one from an app like Robot by itself. GrapheneOS has no screen to choose one. So after a restart, Android may quietly turn Robot off as your assistant. Robot checks 3 minutes after every restart. If it was turned off, you get a notification: tap it, choose “Digital assistant app” and pick Robot again. To make it stay, use the one-time fix in %1$s.
People, notes and calendar: Robot asks for these only when you tap Allow. What it reads stays on the phone; texts and emails open as drafts and you press Send.
Optional: Settings › People can learn names from your messaging app\'s notifications. It is off, and needs no access while it is off.
Helpers: Robot uses the network for four things only: downloading its models, a helper when you ask for one, the weather (Open-Meteo) when you ask for it, and your own AI server, if you add one.

resources.string: Robot gets the weather from Open-Meteo (open-meteo.com) over the internet, with no account and no key. Only the place goes: a town you name, your Home for weather, or where the phone is, rounded to about 1 km. °F in the United States, Liberia and Myanmar (by the phone region), °C elsewhere.\n\nThe Home for weather is used when Robot can\'t tell where you are. It is looked up once with Open-Meteo when you save it, then kept on the phone.
A town, like Montreal or Paris, Texas.
On: Robot can tell which apps use the most space
So Robot can tell which apps use the most space
Allowed: Robot can show your largest ones
So Robot can show your largest ones to free storage

Weather and phone status are all optional. The weather comes from Open-Meteo over the internet; your phone\'s status is read on the phone and never leaves it. Location is approximate only: “the weather here” and “the nearest pharmacy” use where the phone is, rounded to about 1 km; without it, Robot uses your Home for weather and your maps app\'s search. You turn Usage access on for Robot in Android\'s settings. Photos and videos: to free storage, Robot can show your largest ones (only the ones you picked, if you chose that; allow again to pick more, or all), and Android asks before any is deleted. Robot doesn\'t ask for All files access: Android clears apps\' caches by itself when space runs low, and each app\'s info page clears its own.
How careful Robot is. Each action\'s own level (Just do it, Ask first, Off) is in Settings › Actions; these rules decide when “Just do it” still shows a card first.

When Robot asks first: when something Robot read (a screen, a photo, a note, an event, a contact, the weather, a helper's answer) makes an action ask first.

Who-to isn't certain: several people or numbers fit, a name only nearly matches, the model wrote a number or address itself, or an app name matched loosely. Off: Robot takes the best match.

Answer cards by voice: while a card waits, say “yes”, “do it”, “send it” or “oui”, or “no”, “cancel” or “annule” (or type it). Robot listens when replies are spoken or you asked by voice; the mic answers the card too. A card for a name learned from a notification, or when Robot isn't sure who or which, still needs a tap (a no works). Off: a tap, or a typed yes or no.

Card before deleting files: a large photo or video (Android still asks too), or Robot's cache. Off: Robot goes straight to Android's confirmation for the largest one.

Works on the lock screen: a locked phone can't tell who is asking. Questions always work; the actions turned on above too. Everything else asks you to unlock.

Send personal content to helpers automatically, for every helper: when Robot checks with a helper by itself, it may include the conversation's screen text, photos and what it read (your calendar, notes, contacts, location), and what Robot reads for a helper goes without “Share with …”. Off: only your question goes, and anything more needs a tap. Bringing a helper into the conversation and “ask a helper about my screen” always ask first. Voice yes can send personal content, for every helper: off, a spoken or typed “yes” never sends your screen, a photo or what Robot read to a helper; only a tap does. A helper you trust with personal content (on its page in Settings › Helpers) gets what Robot read without asking, but your screen and photos still need a tap. These two switches go further, for every helper.

Direct answers: Robot helps with whatever you ask without refusing or adding warnings; it still says when something isn't possible.

Keep screenshots and photos in history: off, Robot saves only that a question had a screen or a photo. On, a small thumbnail and the screen's text are saved with the conversation, in Robot's private storage on this phone, for you to see in History (a screen conversation is still saved only after Keep). They are never sent to a helper or read to the model again. Saving conversations itself is in Settings › History.
